request.description: Wheat crop at tillering (Zadoks GS 20–29). Field inspection in Foggia reveals very few isolated lesions affecting less than 15% of the canopy. Orange-yellow uredinia with chlorotic halos are visible on the adaxial leaf surface; smaller darker telial pustules are present on the underside, consistent with Puccinia triticina (brown rust). Severity approximately <15% of leaf area. Current meteorological conditions are unknown and must be retrieved via real-time API query before any fungicide application decision can be made.

Wheat crop at stem elongation (Zadoks GS 30–37). Field inspection in Foggia reveals moderate spread with approximately 30–40% of leaf area affected. Orange-yellow uredinia with chlorotic halos are visible on the adaxial leaf surface; smaller darker telial pustules are present on the underside, consistent with Puccinia triticina (brown rust). Severity approximately 30–40% of leaf area. No weather data is available for this location at the time of inspection — live conditions must be checked before proceeding.

Wheat crop at heading (Zadoks GS 50–59). Field inspection in Foggia reveals heavy infection with 50–60% of the canopy showing orange-yellow uredinia. Orange-yellow uredinia with chlorotic halos are visible on the adaxial leaf surface; smaller darker telial pustules are present on the underside, consistent with Puccinia triticina (brown rust). Severity approximately 50–60% of leaf area. The agronomist on site did not record temperature or humidity; real-time weather retrieval is required to assess disease risk.

Severity approximately 60%+ of leaf area. Environmental data (temperature, humidity, wind speed) is unavailable — an API call is required before scheduling treatment.

Tomato crop at vegetative (4–6 true leaves) in Naples. Inspection reveals scattered water-soaked lesions on 2–3 leaves per plant. Brown-black necrotic lesions are confirmed on stems and petioles consistent with Phytophthora infestans (late blight). Diagnosis supported by field assessment. No weather data is available for this location at the time of inspection — live conditions must be checked before proceeding.

Tomato crop at flowering in Naples. Inspection reveals water-soaked lesions on 20–30% of the canopy with white sporulation on leaf undersides. Brown-black necrotic lesions are confirmed on stems and petioles consistent with Phytophthora infestans (late blight). Diagnosis supported by field assessment. The agronomist on site did not record temperature or humidity; real-time weather retrieval is required to assess disease risk.

Tomato crop at early fruit set in Naples. Inspection reveals rapidly expanding brown-black lesions on leaves and stems, white sporulation abundant, fruit infected. Brown-black necrotic lesions are confirmed on stems and petioles consistent with Phytophthora infestans (late blight). Diagnosis supported by field assessment. Environmental data (temperature, humidity, wind speed) is unavailable — an API call is required before scheduling treatment.

Olive grove (pit hardening (July)) in Bari. Fruit sampling confirms Bactrocera oleae infestation: 5–8% oviposition sting rate on sampled fruits, near economic threshold. The agronomist on site did not record temperature or humidity; real-time weather retrieval is required to assess disease risk.

Wheat field at early anthesis (Zadoks GS 60–61) in Bologna. bleaching on 5–10% of spikelets; faint pink-orange sporodochia at spikelet bases on a few heads. Fusarium graminearum (head blight / scab) is the suspected pathogen based on the characteristic bleaching pattern and spore coloration. Fungicide application decision requires assessment of infection-period conditions. Environmental data (temperature, humidity, wind speed) is unavailable — an API call is required before scheduling treatment.
